text:
Carolina arrives at Nassau Coliseum with a four-game winning streak snapped, a 4-1 loss at Nashville on Tuesday where Juuse Saros saved 2.6 goals more than the shots deserved. The Hurricanes are still 4-1-0 in their last five and are missing Jordan Staal, with Jackson Blake taking his spot beside Martinook and Ehlers. The Islanders have been idle since a 4-0 loss to Edmonton on Oct. 31, when Tristan Jarry stopped all 18 shots. They're 2-2-1 in their last five and are without Matias Maccelli, Ryan Pulock and Calum Ritchie.

Our numbers favor Carolina, 3.52 expected goals to 2.58 (expected goals measure the quality of chances). At five on five, the Hurricanes have taken 58% of the expected goals in their games, the Islanders 50%. Carolina's power play creates 0.98 expected goals a game against a New York penalty kill that allows 0.90, and the Islanders take 4.6 penalties a game. In net, projected starter Pyotr Kochetkov is 9.5 goals saved above expected this season (how many more goals he stopped than an average goalie would have on the same shots), while Ilya Sorokin is at 5.6 but posted 22.3 last season.

Watch Blake, on a seven-game point streak, and Sebastian Aho, who has a 35% chance to score. Mark Jankowski has 9 points in his last ten, and the extra chances are real. For New York, Bo Horvat tops the Islanders at 36% to score, and Matthew Schaefer is worth a look on the power play.
